title: Part Three, Chapter 4: Tulanzú and the Gods

verses.t: This is what Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam said; and they said, "Let us wait for the dawn." And they were great sages and men of understanding, very worthy of respect and greatness; and our first fathers and mothers did not yet have gods of wood and stone. And growing tired there of waiting for the sun, and all the peoples with them, those of Yaqui, being already many, with these worthy and venerable men, they said, "Come, let us go and search; let us go and see whether there is any sign of finding what we speak of. For we who stay here have no one to watch over us and guard us." This is what Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam said; and their people heard it and listened, and followed them, and they went away.

And the mountain and place to which Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam went, with those of Ylocab and Tanub, was called Tulanzú ("seven caves and seven ravines"), and so was named the town where they went to get the gods. And they all came to Tulanzú, and the men who went cannot be counted; those who went were many. In good order the gods came out: first for Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam, and rejoicing they said, "Now we have found what we were looking for!" And the first to come out was the god Tohil, hanging on the back of Balam-quitzé, who carried him; and then the god Avilix came out, whom Balam-acab carried; and then the god Hacavitz, whom Mahucutah carried. Nicahtacah was the name of the god that Yquibalam brought out. And only the Quichés went with them, and also those of Tanub; and so the god of the people of Tanub is also the god Tohil. And they took their name from their ancestors, and the people of Tanub are now called lords. And the third were those of Ylocab, whose god likewise was Tohil, whom their ancestors, who were lords, received; and so they know it now.

And so the three Quiché branches were named, and they did not leave or forsake one another, because the god of all of them was one, Tohil of the Quiché, and Tohil of Tanub and Ylocab; the name of their god was only one, and so the three Quiché branches did not divide. And the three were truly great: Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz. And then all the peoples went in: those of Rabinal, the Cakchiquels, those of Quiquinaha, with those of Yaqui, as they are now called. And there the language of the peoples was changed, and they spoke differently and did not understand one another, when they came from Tulanzú; and there they separated. Some went towards the East, and many came here. And they dressed only in skins, because they had not yet found good clothing to put on; only the skins of animals were their adornment. And they were poor and owned nothing; only their being was that of wonder-working men.
